text:
maya: Quick preflight: APAC-west edge cohort maintenance scheduled Tue 02:00-04:00 local (2026-04-07). NIC firmware + microcode patch on GPUs. Low traffic but well be cautious.
sam: How many nodes impacted? need to size reserved capacity impact.
maya: ~180 nodes total across 2 racks. If we cordon cohorts for rolling reboots, expect ~18% transient capacity drop.
andre: Can we cohort by pool to keep burst capacity for latency-sensitive work? prefer pool-first stagger.
jia: Id split into 3: canary (12 nodes), primary (80), secondary (88). Canary validates KV regen and kernel compatibility.
frank: Budget note  backfill from burst pools may cost extra. Rough estimate $500-700/hr if we pull spot capacity.
lucy: Ill flag finance for cost tagging and post-event chargeback.
ops-bot: Maintenance scheduled: APAC-west NIC+GPU microcode. Reminder 30m before.
maya: Runbook summary:
maya: - canary first. run smoke + p95 checks
maya: - abort criteria: latency >1.5x or error rate >0.5%
maya: - after each node reboot, kick KV/prefix cache seed
sam: We should switch routing preference for critical routes to eu-west during cohort-b. TTL 10m.
jia: KV seed command (post-canary warmup):
jia: ```
jia: ./kvseed --cohort=canary --parallel=6 --rate=5000
jia: ```
andre: Drain wrapper we'll use:
andre: ```
andre: ./drain-node --node $NODE --grace-period 120 --eviction-rate 5
andre: ```
frank: CS comms: Dedicated customers need a heads-up about short latency blips. Who owns this?
lucy: Ill prepare a short note and loop in cs-eng. Draft by EOD.
ops-bot: Autoscaler patch merged to canary cluster at 01:14 UTC.
sam: Autoscaler tweak: avoid scaling into these pools during window. Patch config:
sam: ```yaml
sam: autoscaler:
sam:   cooldown: 300
sam:   avoid_pools: ["apac-west-canary","apac-west-primary"]
sam: ```
andre: Proposed rollout timeline:
andre: - 02:00 canary (12 nodes) drain+reboot+smoke tests (~30m)
andre: - 02:40 -> primary (80 nodes) staggered over 40m
andre: - 03:40 -> secondary (88 nodes) finish by ~04:20 if all green
jia: Monitoring checks for oncall:
jia: - pre: baseline snapshot (latency/errs/gpu-temp/egress)
jia: - post-canary: compare KV hitrate & p95
jia: - continuous: model-serving spikes, actor heartbeats
sam: Throttle policy during window: reduce non-critical batch QoS cap 128->64 to protect latency paths.
andre: After each cohort, run prefix-cache prefetch to reduce cold-cache tail; previous run saved ~8% tokens.
jia: Set thermal alert: GPU temp >82C for >2m -> auto-cordon and escalate.
frank: Cost decision: prefer local burst backfill before cross-region failover to avoid egress costs. fallback to eu-west only if necessary.
maya: Oncall please be available 01:45-04:30 local for quick actions. Ill post canary results here.
sam: Ack.
jia: Ack.
andre: Ack.
frank: Ack.
lucy: Ack.
ops-bot: Reminder 30m: APAC-west maintenance (canary first).
